from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p=Path('tmp/pdfs');p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    txt=page.extract_text()
    (p/f'page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(txt)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'PAGE {i}\\n'+page.extract_text() for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1)))
print((p/'page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

strengths: Significance: Repeatedly solving related MIPs is an important practical setting. PreMIO offers a simple interface between learned predictions and commercial solvers through two cardinality constraints. The four complementary regions preserve exhaustive search when all branches are solved correctly.

Empirical promise: Figure 1 reports substantial primal time-to-target improvements across knapsack, set covering, and simulated unit commitment, using both Gurobi and COPT. Improvements also occur with default solver heuristics, supporting the method's potential practical usefulness.

Presentation: The problem setting, assumptions, pseudocode, and distinction between primal heuristics and exhaustive branching are organized clearly. The manuscript provides hardware information, data-generation procedures, training budgets, and several solver settings.

Limitations and ethics: Remark 6 acknowledges that exact posterior estimation is unrealistic, and Section 4.4 discusses infeasible neighborhoods and parameter sensitivity. These disclosures are valuable. No material research-ethics concern is apparent from the benchmark and simulated-data experiments.
weaknesses: Soundness: Theorem 2's central concentration argument is not justified. Appendix B.4 uses unconditional correctness probabilities for sums over U and L, although these subsets are selected by predictions on the same random test instance. A3 does not justify this selection step. For example, an all-zero optimal solution with independent rare false-positive predictions can have high marginal classification accuracy while every coordinate selected into U is incorrect. The stated assumptions therefore do not establish the claimed high-probability containment guarantee.

Soundness: Remark 4 and Appendix B.1 incorrectly claim that disjoint training datasets imply independent prediction errors on a shared test instance. Equation (4) factors an integral of a product without establishing the necessary independence over the instance distribution; non-overlapping feature segments alone do not suffice either. The practical use of Theorem 3 additionally substitutes logistic predictions for exact conditional means without reporting held-out calibration, error dependence, or neighborhood-containment measurements.

Soundness: Section 3.2 reverses the pruning condition. If the preferred region excludes every global optimizer, a complementary region contains a better solution and cannot be infeasible under the proposed incumbent cutoff. Even when the preferred region contains the optimum, complementary integer infeasibility does not imply LP infeasibility. The exhaustive partition remains useful, but the explanation that certification often costs only three LP solves needs correction and stronger supporting evidence.

Evaluation: The MIPLIB improvement is calculated on 57 of 132 instances after excluding infeasible restricted neighborhoods and cases where both runs time out. This establishes conditional performance on the retained subset, without quantifying overall failure rates or fallback costs. Results on the full collection are needed to support general solver improvement. Table 3 contains only 30 entries, including a repeated blp-ar98, so the reported 57-instance aggregate cannot be audited from the supplied results.

Evaluation and significance: Section 4.2 measures time to a target selected from PreMIO's own 120-second run. This is informative for primal search, but matched-budget objective gaps and handling of unreachable targets are missing. SCUC has only five test instances per regime, uncertainty estimates are absent, and exhaustive branching is evaluated on only 20 knapsack instances. These results do not yet establish broad, reliable improvements in solution quality or optimality certification.

Originality: The manuscript itself identifies prediction-distance cuts and local branching as related work. Its two cardinality constraints impose separate budgets on the two components of distance from a predicted assignment. This could be a useful refinement, but there is no comparison using the same predictor with standard prediction-based local branching, nor an ablation comparing concentration-derived thresholds against tuned neighborhood sizes. Consequently, the distinctive benefit of the proposed integration remains unestablished.

Presentation and reproducibility: Appendix D defines its 'accuracy' quantities using error indicators and then recommends maximizing them; it also selects tau approximately 0.1 despite the stated range [0.5, 1]. The displayed first group in Table 1 gives shifted geometric means of approximately 36.6 and 32.1 under the stated 10-second shift, rather than 28.7 and 25.8. Exact solver versions, random seeds, logistic-regression training settings, and runnable code/data artifacts are not identified. These issues materially impede reproduction of the tuning procedure and reported results.
